body.statement: The sharp identified set for the entire threshold-loss vector is exactly \(\mathcal V(p_{BT},q)\), and for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^{|\mathcal M|}\) its support function equals \(h_{\mathcal V}(\lambda)\) in \(\text{def:support-function}\). The same common-plan representation gives the signed pairwise derivation \(D_{mj}=\pi[\max_{x\in\Gamma_H(p,q)}\sum_{b=m}^{j-1}\sum_w w x_{bw}-\sum_{b=m}^{j-1}\mu_b]\) for \(m<j\), \(D_{mj}=\pi[\sum_{b=j}^{m-1}\mu_b-\min_{x\in\Gamma_H(p,q)}\sum_{b=j}^{m-1}\sum_w w x_{bw}]\) for \(m>j\), and \(D_{mm}=0\). Hence an off-diagonal \(D_{mj}\) may be negative, \(R_m=\max_{j\in\mathcal M}D_{mj}\ge0\), and \(\mathcal M^\star=\operatorname*{argmin}_{m\in\mathcal M}R_m\) is the complete deterministic minimax correspondence. In particular, optimizing coordinates separately generally produces a strict outer rectangle rather than the joint identified set.
body.justification: All candidate thresholds are functions of one latent switched law, so the theorem identifies their joint geometry and derives signed pairwise regret and every deterministic minimax threshold from that same law.
body.gap: JanvinRyalenSarvetStensrud2025 bounds one threshold and MontielOleaQiuStoye2026 analyzes joint payoff restrictions in a Gaussian decision experiment; neither identifies the common-coupling threshold-value polytope.
body.consumer: A clinician choosing among several prespecified switching thresholds obtains the exact feasible loss vectors and every robust deterministic threshold, including ties, rather than combining incompatible marginal extrema.
